title: Support Vector Machine Approaches to Sentiment Classification
abstract: This paper studies support vector machine classifiers for sentiment analysis. A support vector machine trained with a linear kernel method on tf idf features performs text classification on the imdb review corpus. The kernel method provides large margin separators, and the support vector machine generalizes well on reviews.

title: Kernel Methods for Opinion Mining with Support Vector Machines
abstract: Opinion mining is tackled with a support vector machine and a kernel method over bag of words features. The kernel method maps sentiment analysis features into a reproducing kernel space. The support vector machine kernel method combination outperforms naive bayes on text classification benchmarks.

title: Comparing Kernel Functions for Support Vector Machine Text Categorization
abstract: We compare linear, polynomial and radial basis kernel method choices for support vector machine text categorization. Each kernel method is evaluated for sentiment analysis accuracy. The support vector machine with a polynomial kernel method gives the best text classification trade off.

title: Feature Engineering for Support Vector Machine Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Feature engineering remains central to support vector machine sentiment analysis. We design n gram and negation features for the kernel method input space. The support vector machine with the engineered kernel method features improves text classification accuracy on sst.

title: A Polynomial Kernel Method for Document Classification
abstract: A polynomial kernel method is proposed for support vector machine document classification. The kernel method captures feature conjunctions that linear support vector machine configurations miss. Experiments on sentiment analysis corpora confirm the kernel method advantage for text classification.

title: Large Margin Kernel Machines for Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Large margin kernel method training is revisited for support vector machine sentiment analysis. The support vector machine objective is optimized with a smoothed kernel method loss. On six text classification datasets the kernel method sets a new support vector machine reference point.

title: Support Vector Machines with String Kernels for Short Text Classification
abstract: Short text classification is addressed with a support vector machine over a string kernel method. The kernel method compares character subsequences of posts. The support vector machine string kernel method pairing improves sentiment analysis of microblog text classification.

title: Kernel Method Ensembles for Opinion Classification
abstract: An ensemble of kernel method classifiers is built on support vector machine base learners. Each support vector machine uses a different kernel method bandwidth. The kernel method ensemble raises sentiment analysis accuracy for text classification across domains.

title: Sentiment Classification with Support Vector Machine and Linguistic Features
abstract: Linguistic features are combined with a support vector machine kernel method for sentiment classification. Part of speech and dependency features enrich the kernel method input. The support vector machine keeps a clear margin on the imdb text classification benchmark.

title: Revisiting Kernel Methods for Large Scale Text Classification
abstract: We revisit the kernel method for large scale text classification with a support vector machine. Approximate kernel method expansions keep support vector machine training tractable. The kernel method remains competitive for sentiment analysis at the million document scale.

title: Support Vector Machine versus Naive Bayes for Sentiment Analysis
abstract: A controlled comparison of support vector machine and naive bayes for sentiment analysis is presented. The support vector machine with a linear kernel method dominates on text classification accuracy. The kernel method gap widens with more training data.

title: Deep Neural Network Models for Sentiment Classification
abstract: A deep neural network is trained end to end for sentiment classification. The deep neural network composes word embedding vectors for text classification. The deep neural network removes the need for hand crafted kernel method features.

title: Convolutional Network Architectures for Text Categorization
abstract: A convolutional network is applied to text categorization. The convolutional network filters act as a deep neural network feature extractor over word embedding inputs. This deep neural network convolutional network design improves sentiment analysis accuracy.

title: A Deep Neural Network with Word Embeddings for Document Classification
abstract: Word embedding pretraining feeds a deep neural network for document classification. The deep neural network stacks convolutional network and pooling layers. This deep neural network becomes the standard text classification reference.

title: Convolutional Neural Network Sentence Classifier
abstract: A convolutional network sentence classifier is described. The convolutional network is a deep neural network over word embedding channels. The deep neural network convolutional network design sets strong sentiment analysis results on sst.

title: Recurrent Deep Neural Network for Opinion Mining
abstract: A recurrent deep neural network with lstm cells is used for opinion mining. The deep neural network encodes word embedding sequences. The recurrent deep neural network complements convolutional network designs for text classification.

title: Attention-Augmented Convolutional Network for Text Classification
abstract: An attention augmented convolutional network is proposed for text classification. The convolutional network features feed a deep neural network attention layer. The deep neural network convolutional network hybrid improves sentiment analysis.

title: Deep Neural Network Ensembles for Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Deep neural network ensembles combine convolutional network and recurrent members for sentiment analysis. Each deep neural network votes on the text classification label. The deep neural network ensemble raises accuracy on imdb and sst.

title: Character-level Convolutional Network for Text Classification
abstract: A character level convolutional network is designed for text classification. The convolutional network is a deep neural network that reads raw characters. The deep neural network convolutional network design removes tokenization for sentiment analysis.

title: Improving Convolutional Network Text Classifiers with Pretraining
abstract: Pretraining improves a convolutional network text classifier. The convolutional network deep neural network is first pretrained on unlabeled reviews. The deep neural network then fine tunes for sentiment analysis text classification.

title: Deep Neural Network Regularization for Document Classification
abstract: Regularization techniques for deep neural network document classification are surveyed. Dropout and label smoothing stabilize the deep neural network. The convolutional network variant benefits most for sentiment analysis text classification.

title: Pretrained Language Model Fine-tuning for Sentiment Analysis
abstract: A pretrained language model is fine tuned for sentiment analysis. The pretrained language model is a transformer with multi head self attention layers. Fine tuning the pretrained language model transformer surpasses earlier supervised baselines on text classification.

title: Transformer Self-Attention for Document Classification
abstract: A transformer encoder with multi head self attention is used for document classification. The self attention transformer replaces hand tuned feature extractors entirely. The transformer self attention design improves text classification on long reviews.

title: Pretrained Language Model Transfer for Opinion Mining
abstract: Transfer from a pretrained language model is studied for opinion mining. The pretrained language model transformer multi head self attention layers adapt with little labeled data. The pretrained language model gives strong text classification accuracy.

title: Self-Attention Transformer Variants for Text Classification
abstract: Efficient transformer multi head self attention variants are compared for text classification. Sparse self attention lowers transformer compute cost. Each transformer self attention variant is evaluated on sentiment analysis benchmarks.

title: Foundation Model Prompting for Sentiment Classification
abstract: A foundation model is prompted for sentiment classification. The foundation model is a large transformer pretrained with self attention at scale. Prompting the foundation model avoids fine tuning for text classification.

title: Evaluating Foundation Model Zero-shot Text Classification
abstract: Zero shot text classification with a foundation model is evaluated. The foundation model transformer uses self attention over instructions. The foundation model rivals fine tuned transformer baselines on sentiment analysis.

title: Instruction Tuning of Foundation Model for Opinion Mining
abstract: Instruction tuning aligns a foundation model for opinion mining. The foundation model is a transformer trained with self attention on instructions. The tuned foundation model improves text classification robustness.

title: Foundation Model Fine-tuning versus Prompting for Sentiment
abstract: Fine tuning and prompting of a foundation model are compared for sentiment analysis. The foundation model transformer self attention backbone is shared. Prompting the foundation model is cheaper while fine tuning is steadier for text classification.

title: Efficient Self-Attention Transformer for Long Documents
abstract: An efficient self attention transformer is proposed for long documents. Linear self attention reduces transformer memory. The transformer self attention design keeps text classification accuracy on long sentiment analysis corpora.
